narrative.firing_model: a review is requested only when the best job's weighted on-time gain clears the bar: gain = w_j*(p1-p0) - REVIEW_BAR, with p1 = P(start+1+next-prefix residual <= due), p0 = P(start+prefix <= due). At alpha=1 the reservation error b-p = alpha*(Q_res - eps) makes the point forecast cancel, so a second look only sharpens the residual distribution, whose sd is already ~0.4-0.7 s.
narrative.price_channel: every review spends 1 s of a 100-125 s horizon (the fleet idles) and 1 unit of a 32-40 unit budget; the marginal on-time cost of the delay is phi(delta/sigma)/sigma per second on the reviewed job.
narrative.why_gate_unreachable: free perfect 1.0-prefix information at t=0 (no delay, no cost, unlimited) reaches at most +0.42 pt; the paid arm is that same information minus 1 s and minus 1 cost unit, so it cannot beat the free arm. Only knowing the true durations (oracle) reaches +5.6..+10.5 pt, which is not an information a second observation can deliver.
narrative.degenerate_trigger_arms: all VoI-gated and window-gated arms fire <0.05 reviews per trial at the headline mapping, so they are numerically indistinguishable from no-review: the event of 'a review is worth paying for' almost never occurs. The greedy arm fires 6-8 reviews and loses 5.7 pt on average.

information_ceiling.definition: free, instantaneous, unlimited perfect prefix observation at t=0 under the same reservation rule: an information superset of any paid-review policy restricted to that rule, at zero delay and zero cost
information_ceiling.conclusion: free perfect 1.0-prefix information never clears 1.0 pt (max +0.42 pt); the full-duration oracle clears it everywhere (+5.6 to +10.5 pt). The paid arm is priced strictly worse than the free one, so the review lever cannot clear the gate.
